Add the shared Next.js site shell, design tokens, dark and light themes, keyboard command palette and tool registry. Planned tools point to package locations. The footer displays the full public DID, fingerprint, licence and build commit.

## Why

Tool agents need a stable shell and a single registry entry to publish their pages. The first milestone names unimplemented data and verification features directly instead of showing sample results.

## Checks

- Strict types, ESLint, two registry contract tests and production build pass.
- Chromium at 1440x1000 and 390x844 checks palette search, arrows, Escape, themes, titles and footer navigation. Reduced motion is enabled for mobile. No page errors or horizontal overflow were observed. Evidence: browser.json and shots/.
- Local production server readiness measured 386 ms after shared-tooling integration. This is a local start measurement, not hosted latency.
- Fresh clone and final gate logs accompany this milestone.
- Live devnet data and cryptographic verification are the next milestone. They are not verified by this shell.
